subject: Capacity runway scenarios for Brightline pilot - ask and ops constraints
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@brightlinelabs.io>; procurement@brightlinelabs.io
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity runway scenarios for Brightline pilot - ask and ops constraints

Team —

Brightline is ready to move from an API pilot to a week-long live pilot in late June (see attached forecast). They asked for a short-term dedicated runway to guarantee latencies for checkout flows. I want to capture a few possible capacity scenarios so Product and Ops can sign off on an exception and we can communicate deployment timelines to procurement.

Quick context: Brightline anticipates 10k–30k inference calls/day with traffic concentrated in 6–8 hour windows; peak concurrency estimates in the forecast are ~220 concurrent sessions with bursts to ~400 for 20–30s. They asked for a 3-day reserved fallback plus autoscale headroom if usage spikes.

Please respond with: (1) conservative / mid / aggressive GPU allocation scenarios (N GPUs + expected throughput), (2) feasible autoscale exception window and duration for the pilot, (3) any safety constraints (prefix cache sizing, KV persistence), and (4) a short ops checklist for a temporary reserved lane (what we need from procurement and Brightline).

Attachments: brightline_q2_traffic_forecast.xlsx (forecast + sample traces), brightline_map_proposal_v1.pdf (pilot MAP draft).

Sergio
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity runway scenarios for Brightline pilot - ask and ops constraints

Thanks for the primer, Sergio. I reviewed the attachment quickly — couple clarifying Qs before we size:

- Is Brightline willing to accept a soft SLA (SLO w/ credits) for the pilot or do they require a firm SLA? Procurement mentioned they prefer a commitment but can accept short pilot guardrails.
- Are the 20–30s bursts expected to be sustained over many users (i.e., many sessions spiking synchronously) or tied to a small set of heavy calls? That changes batching behavior and KV cache pressure.

If they can accept a pilot SLO with explicit fallback to a lower-cost model variant for non-critical calls, we can propose a smaller reserved runway plus a short autoscale cushion.

I'll draft a simple MAP and share a proposed SLO clause; Marcus/Hannah — can you sketch 3 scenarios with rough cost delta (per-hour) so procurement has numbers?

—Laura
PM, Redwood Console
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 13:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity runway scenarios for Brightline pilot - ask and ops constraints

Notes from infra POV — initial sizing off the forecast and a conservative tactical plan: 

- Conservative: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (steady throughput ~1200 tokens/s combined), fallback to host model variant at 75% quality for non-checkout calls. Estimated burn: ~$19.50/hr.
- Mid: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (steady throughput ~2400 tokens/s, headroom for 450 concurrent short bursts). Estimated burn: ~$36/hr.
- Aggressive: 6x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (steady throughput ~3600 tokens/s, comfortable for 400+ concurrent bursts). Estimated burn: ~$52/hr.

Autoscale exception proposal: we can open a constrained autoscale window +1 GPUs for 2h/day for the pilot (manual trigger or schedule). Longer windows require pre-approval from capacity planning; anything >4h/day will impact other pilots.

Operational constraints / risk: prefix cache needs to be warmed before main window (we should schedule a warmup run 1–2 hrs prior); KV footprint for Brightline sessions ~8–12GB — recommend reserving an extra 12GB KV pool for the lane. If Brightline’s forecast underestimates burstiness, we should be prepared to degrade to the cheaper variant with clear customer messaging.

I'll add an ops checklist and a short runbook to the Jira ticket INF-4123.

—Marcus
Infra Eng Lead, Serving Runtime
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@brightlinelabs.io>; procurement@brightlinelabs.io
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity runway scenarios for Brightline pilot - ask and ops constraints

Adding operational details:

- Temporary reserved lane request: we can approve a 72-hour reserved runway with a 2x or 4x GPU profile. For short pilots we prefer timeboxed reservations rather than open-ended carveouts.
- Autoscale exception: policy allows 2 one-off autoscale bursts/day up to +50% capacity for pilots with product sign-off; exceptions beyond that require Capacity Council review. For Brightline, I'd approve 2 bursts/day for up to 90 minutes each (manual ops trigger).
- Procurement asks: we need a signed MAP that states run dates, reserved GPU profile, alerting contacts, and rollback criteria. Also request Brightline to sign an ops acknowledgment about accepting degraded fallback behavior in the event of unexpected overload.

I'll attach the ops checklist as a short doc to INF-4123 and flag capacity planning.

—Hannah
SRE Manager
From: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@brightlinelabs.io>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlinelabs.io
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity runway scenarios for Brightline pilot - ask and ops constraints

Thanks for the fast turn. A few answers and commitments from Brightline: 

- We can accept a pilot SLO with defined rollback and credits for missed SLOs. Firm SLA is not required for this short test.
- The 20–30s bursts are tied to synchronous checkout steps across a subset of users — we've seen short synchronized spikes during marketing promos. We can provide request traces if that helps.
- For the pilot we prefer the mid-profile (4x GPUs) plus the 2 daily autoscale bursts (up to +1 GPU) you proposed. That should give us headroom without a large commitment.
- Procurement: we can sign the MAP with the dates 2026-06-23 to 2026-06-25 and accept the ops acknowledgment. Please send the MAP and the pricing numbers so our procurement team can finish the short agreement.

Claire Zhao
Head of Platform Partnerships
Brightline Labs
